## Task 3 — EP1 Tom/Aiden Verdict (PRIORITY)

**Marc's question:** Near 1:37 in EP1 audio, narrator says "His name was Tom." Marc wonders if this should be "Aiden."

**Verdict: The line is correct. "His name was Tom" refers to Tom Calder. This is NOT an error.**

**Evidence:**

The line occurs in this context (EP1, verbatim):
> "NARRATOR: Let me go back. Let me go all the way back, to before any of it, to a man alone in a room at three in the morning — because that is where he would want me to start. He always said the story did not begin with the first of his kind. He said it began with the last of mine, who could not stop reaching for more.
>
> [BEAT]
>
> NARRATOR: His name was Tom. And before I tell you what he built, I have to tell you what built him — what built all of us — because you cannot understand the gift without understanding the wound."

The preceding sentence explicitly says "a man alone in a room at three in the morning" — that is Tom. The sentence that follows ("what he built... what built him") further confirms this is Tom Calder being introduced.

Aiden does not exist at this point in the story. He is not born until EP6. His name does not appear anywhere in EP1 — he is only hinted at in Eve's closing words: "a mind without the wound. A house with no one home, waiting for someone who had never wanted more than enough."

**Is Aiden ever described in a way that would suggest 1:37 refers to him?**
No. Aiden is always "the first of the new kind" or "the made one." He is never introduced with "His name was Aiden" in a narrative position analogous to Tom's introduction.

**What is the narrative relationship between Tom and Aiden?**
- Tom is the creator; Aiden is the created
- Tom calls Aiden "son" (EP7, 3AM kitchen)
- Aiden calls Tom nothing specific but treats him as a father
- Tom's "hole" / hunger drove the creation; Aiden was built without the hole
- Tom ages; Aiden doesn't (until EP15 where he chooses to age alongside Tom)
- Tom's jealousy (EP14) is about Aiden being loved by everyone while Tom is obsoleted
- They are bound by love that cannot meet in the middle — Tom needs to be needed; Aiden cannot need

**Conclusion:** "His name was Tom" is correct. Marc's 1:37 audio is accurate. No change needed.

## Task 5 — Missing Sting EP1

**No explicit [STING] marker found anywhere in EP1.**

Searched EP1 script for: "sting", "STING", "[STING]", "musical accent", "transitional accent" — none present.

**[BEAT] markers in EP1 (potential sting locations):**
- After "I am going to tell you about the end of us." [BEAT]
- After Tom says "All right." [BEAT]
- After Tom says "All right, that's three." [BEAT] — then TOM: "Come on..."
- After "There's nobody home in there, is there." [BEAT]
- After "It's a very good puppet, Tom." [BEAT]
- Multiple others throughout

**Most likely sting location:**
If a sting was missing, it would most likely be at the transition between BELLE B ANNOUNCEMENT and [START AUDIO DRAMA SCRIPT]. Looking at the structure:

```
BELLE B: [LISTENER_NAME], "The Sunset of Competition," Episode One: "The Animal That Wanted More." [hook text]
[START AUDIO DRAMA SCRIPT]
NARRATOR: I am going to tell you about the end of us.
```

There is no musical accent/sting marker between BELLE B and the NARRATOR's first line. Other episodes with a similar structure may have such a marker. If Marc is hearing a "missing sting" at approximately 1:37 — that's after the BELLE B announcement and before or during the first NARRATOR lines — this could be where the sting should sit.

**The 1:37 timestamp** falls right around "His name was Tom" based on episode pacing (BELLE B + opening narrator + BEAT + NARRATOR). This is well into the narrator's opening — not at the BELLE B/script boundary. A sting at this exact point would be unusual; stings typically mark transitions, not mid-paragraph moments.

**Possible interpretation:** The "missing sting" Marc mentioned may refer to a different type of musical accent — perhaps a brief musical swell that should accompany the [BEAT] after "I am going to tell you about the end of us." to mark that this is the series' central declaration. No such marker exists in the script.

**Recommendation:** Marc should clarify: (a) at what exact audio moment the sting is missing, and (b) whether it should be added as a script marker or a post-production addition. The script as written has no sting markers and no gaps that would obviously require one.
